source: Aria Networks — Closing conversation: Deep Networking and token economics; Aria vs Arista's rise in the cloud era; NeoCloud and accelerator vendors
summary: Technological discontinuities combined with first-principles thinking are the pattern behind outsized investment returns
summary_extended: Baker articulates a repeatable investment framework: outsized returns come when a technological discontinuity is approached from first principles rather than incrementally. He cites his own successful investments in Nvidia (GPUs repurposed from graphics math to deep learning) and Arista (Ethernet-first architecture for cloud networking) as historical proof points, and adds Tesla's battery-floor placement as another example of first-principles engineering unlocking a discontinuity. Baker implies that AI networking represents the current live instance of this pattern, and that the opportunity has not yet been fully exploited — positioning Aria Networks as the present-day analog to what Arista was in the cloud era. The investment implication is that identifying companies attacking a genuine technological discontinuity from first principles, rather than iterating on legacy architectures, is the reliable source of multi-year compounding returns.
detail: Baker articulates his investment framework: GPUs (graphics math → deep learning), Tesla EVs (battery placement), and now AI networking all follow the same pattern — a technological discontinuity that someone approaches from first principles rather than incrementally. He implies Aria fits this pattern and that the AI networking discontinuity has not yet been fully exploited.
confidence_evidence: Baker explicitly states this is 'just that simple' and applies it consistently across multiple historical examples including his own successful investments in Arista and Nvidia.
